question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution:
The correct answer is "**are drawing**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Are drawing**" is in the **present continuous tense**.
 
• Present continuous tense is used to denote an **on going action**.
 
 
• **Example:** *The family is **driving** to Texas. *
 
 
 
• As the action **has not been completed** as is **continuing** still, "are drawing" is the appropriate option. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present tense** can be divided into **simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous.**
 
• **Simple present tense** - denotes a **regular action** .
 
 
• **Example:** *The baby cries for milk.*
 
 
 
• **Present continuous tense** - denotes an **on going action** .
 
 
• **Example: ***The baby is crying for milk.*
 
 
 
• **Present perfect tense** - denotes a **past action** that still **affects the present** .
 
 
• **Example:** *The baby has cried for milk.*
 
 
 
• **Present perfect continuous tense** - denotes an action that was **started in the past** and is still **being continued**. 
 
 
• **Example: ***The baby has been crying for milk.*
